content.content:
refactor(hooks)!: remove local_dev mode

Local-dev mode pointed installed hooks at `scripts/entire-dev`, a launcher
inside the working tree that compiled and ran the checked-out source. It was
read from the *committed* `.entire/settings.json` (settings.go merged
`local_dev` from the project scope, and strategy/common.go regenerated the git
hook from it), so any repository could commit `"local_dev": true` and have
`entire enable` install hooks that execute that repository's own code. A branch
checkout could then swap what ran. This repo shipped exactly that: `local_dev:
true` was tracked, and all six committed agent configs invoked the launcher.

Hooks now always name the `entire` binary. Removed the `--local-dev` flags
(including the non-hidden one on `entire agent add`), `EnableOptions.LocalDev`,
the `localDev` parameter from `Agent.InstallHooks` across all nine agents and
the external-agent protocol, the claude-code local-dev SessionEnd timeout, and
the launcher script.

`EntireSettings.LocalDev` stays as a documented no-op: the loaders use
DisallowUnknownFields, so deleting the field would make every existing settings
file containing `local_dev` a hard parse error. It is not merged from overrides
and nothing reads it, matching the `Strategy` precedent.

Removing the feature is not enough to disarm existing installs, so this also
fixes how hooks written by older versions get replaced:

- `isGitHookInstalledInHooksDir` only looked for the Entire marker, which a
  legacy hook still carries. It therefore read as installed forever and
  EnsureSetup never reinstalled it — while the script it invoked no longer
  existed. Repo-relative prefixes got no availability guard and pre-push
  deliberately propagates exit codes, so that state rejects `git push`. A hook
  naming the legacy launcher now counts as not installed.
- claudecode, factoryaidroid and copilotcli only dropped Entire hooks under
  `--force`, so a plain enable added the current hook beside the legacy one and
  both fired. cursor and codex returned early whenever the current command was
  present, leaving a legacy hook next to it. Stale hooks are now dropped on
  every install, through one shared `agent.DropStaleManagedHooks` primitive
  rather than six per-agent re-derivations (`dupl` cannot see duplication across
  packages, which is how the two divergent copies survived).
- geminicli's idempotency check sampled only SessionStart, so a stale hook on
  any of the other ten types survived every non-force install.
- The write now happens when only a drop occurred: a config can hold both a
  stale and a current hook, where nothing needs adding.
- Every hook prefix is guarded by an existence test. The unguarded path existed
  only for the repo-relative launcher, and was still reachable for unusual
  absolute paths — exactly where losing the guard hurts most.

Regenerates this repo's six committed agent configs through the real install
path. The pi extension had also drifted far enough to be missing the
ENTIRE_PI_NESTED subagent guard that was already in its template, so
`testutil.AssertCommittedDogfoodFile` and `AssertCommittedDogfoodConfigStable`
now fail in CI on drift instead of waiting for someone to notice.
